chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiya ibn Wahb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you enter a town and intend to stay for ten days, complete the prayer upon arrival; and if you intend less than ten days, shorten [the prayer] between you and a month; so when the month is complete, complete the prayer."
He said: I said, 'I entered a town on the first day of Ramadan and I do not intend to stay ten [days].' He said, 'Shorten [the prayer] and fast.'

I said, 'But I remained like that, saying tomorrow or the day after, so I will fast the entire month and shorten [the prayer].' He said, 'Yes, they are one; when you shorten, you fast, and when you fast, you shorten.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayer and fasting when traveling for less than ten days?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential link between the rules of travel prayer (qasr) and fasting, establishing that the condition for shortening prayer simultaneously exempts the traveler from fasting. It highlights the Shia scholarly consensus that the ten-day stay rule applies to both obligations, ensuring consistency in the traveler's legal status. The hadith serves as a practical guide for travelers to determine their religious duties based on their intended duration of residence.
